structure: Part 6, MDM ports of entry. Read in full: PortsOfEntryController.java (one GET handler at /mdm/trade/bcp/poes taking the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and an optional system parameter, answering the fixture loaded at start-up with the shared trace header), PortsOfEntryControllerTest.java (three tests: whole list in MDM order, traffic types, missing key refused), MdmStubResponses.java (the header name and trace-header helper, used here; the shared plumbing itself is part 2's), MdmStubRequests.java (the test helper that adds the key), and portsOfEntryResponse.json (a result array of 78 port records, 16 lines each, with id, activeFrom, activeTo, code, name, townCity, county, postCode, countryCode, traffic and status). Claims 001-036 cover the endpoint, its header and parameter, the response shape, counts of traffic types (Airport 18, Port 59, Rail 1) and statuses (all active, Approved-Live), the empty-field, duplicate-name and odd-copy records, each test, and three gaps. Claims 037-114 are one per port record, in saved order.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes with the list of ports of entry.
The ports of entry call must carry an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header.
The stub accepts any value in the subscription key header: the handler never reads the value, and the tests send "any-value-at-all".
claims.note: The value is bound to a parameter the method body does not use.

claims.statement: A ports of entry call with no subscription key header is refused with 400 Bad Request.
The ports of entry call takes an optional system query parameter.
The system parameter changes nothing: the stub answers the same records whatever system is named, or none.
claims.note: The system parameter is bound but never used in the body.

claims.statement: The ports of entry call answers 200 OK.
The ports of entry response carries the header x-ms-middleware-request-id with the value stub-trace-id.
claims.note: The shared trace-header helper is part 2's to claim; this claim records only that this endpoint uses it.

claims.statement: The stub answers the saved port records whole: every record, unfiltered and unchanged, in the order they are saved.
The stub reads the saved port records once, when it starts, and answers every call from that copy.
claims.note: mechanism: loads the ports fixture into memory at start-up; a change to the file needs a restart.

claims.statement: The ports of entry response body is an object whose result field holds the array of port records.
The stub returns 78 port records.
Each port record has the fields id, activeFrom, activeTo, code, name, townCity, county, postCode, countryCode, traffic and status, and status has a code and a description.
claims.note: Every one of the 78 records has exactly this set of keys.

claims.statement: Each port record carries a UUID as its id.

The records come in MDM's saved order, not sorted: 11 airports first, then 38 ports by name from Aberdeen Harbour to Tilbury Port, then the Folkestone rail record, then 28 further records sorted by code from GB AVO to GB TIL.
claims.note: Read from the record order in the file; the test title calls it MDM order. A consumer that wants the list sorted must sort it itself.

claims.statement: The records hold three traffic types: Airport on 18 records, Port on 59 and Rail on 1.
claims.note: Counted with jq over the whole result array.

claims.statement: Every one of the 78 records has the status code active with the description Approved-Live.
claims.note: Counted with jq: one status value across all 78.

claims.statement: No record sets activeFrom or activeTo: both are null on all 78.
Every record has the countryCode GB.
29 records have an empty townCity, county and postCode: Tilbury Port and the 28 records from GB AVO to GB TIL.
Pembroke Port (GB PED) has a county and postcode but an empty townCity.
Heysham Port (GB HYM), Portsmouth Port (GB PME) and Southampton Port (GB SOU) have a townCity and postcode but an empty county.
Port codes are GB, a space and three or four letters, except Port of Sheerness at GBSHS, which has no space.
Two records are named Port of Sheerness, with the codes GBSHS and GB SHS.
claims.note: A list that shows names alone shows this name twice.

claims.statement: Two records are named Pembroke Port, with the codes GB PED and GB PEM.
claims.note: A list that shows names alone shows this name twice.

claims.statement: Dover has three records: Port of Dover (Eastern) GB DVRE, Port of Dover (Western) GB DVRW and Port of Dover GB DVR.
Tilbury has three records: Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal GB TILR, Tilbury Port GB TILL and TILBURY GB TIL, the last named in capitals.
The Folkestone rail record (GB FOL) gives Felixstowe, Suffolk, IP11 3SY as its town, county and postcode, the same as Felixstowe Port.
claims.note: Recorded as saved; the town looks copied from Felixstowe Port. Not reconciled.

claims.statement: Portsmouth Port's name is saved with two spaces between its words.
The GB TEE record is named Teestort.
claims.note: Possibly a misspelling of Teesport; recorded as saved.

claims.statement: Test getPortsOfEntry_shouldAnswerMdmsPortRecordsWholeInMdmOrder proves the call answers 200 with the stub trace header and 78 records, the first being GB DYC, an Airport in Aberdeen with the status Approved-Live.
Test getPortsOfEntry_shouldCarryEveryPortsTraffic proves GB FOL is the only Rail record and that 18 records are Airport.
Test getPortsOfEntry_shouldRefuseTheCall_whenTheSubscriptionKeyHeaderIsMissing proves a call with no subscription key is answered 400 Bad Request.
No test proves the count of Port records (59), the order beyond the first record, or that the system parameter changes nothing.
claims.note: Looked through all three tests in the class.

claims.statement: The stub holds no port that is inactive, not yet active or no longer active, so a consumer's handling of a status other than Approved-Live, or of activeFrom and activeTo dates, cannot be exercised against it.
The stub cannot be made to fail the ports of entry call other than by leaving out the subscription key: it has no error, empty or slow answer for a consumer to test against.
claims.note: Looked at the controller and its tests; any perf-mode latency is outside this part.
